gary_2026_09_02_frontier_table_nyc_ai_fo.title: Frontier Table NYC: AI Founder Dinner
gary_2026_09_02_frontier_table_nyc_ai_fo.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_09_02_frontier_table_nyc_ai_fo.summary: Gary's Guide: An Evening on the AI Frontier - New York A Frontier Table Dinner, hosted by Obvious AI is changing how we build products at a dizzying rate. But it's also transforming how we build teams, companies, & even startup ecosystems. And the implications are moving faster than the conversation around them. This raises questions that matter more than whether to use Claude Code or Codex. What if the way we've built companies for the last 15 years is entirely incompatible with what's needed for the next 15? What constitutes a moat anymore? What does defensibility look like when anyone can build anything? When you're building at the epicenter of AI acceleration - where capital, talent, & ambition are concentrated at unprecedented scale - how do you build something durable instead of just fast? How do we separate what's meaningful from what's hype when everything is changing this fast? These are also the hardest questions to answer, because the answers are emerging & changing in near real time. And there is rarely space to engage them with peers living through the same transformation & operating on the frontier. So this dinner is an attempt to create that space & facilitate these discussions. The format is simple. A small table, great food, & a few hours to think out loud together. We'll open by sharing the model of the near future driving how we operate at Obvious, the one we're working backwards from. Then we'll turn it over to the room. What we'd ask of everyone is the same thing we'll offer: the fundamental observation driving you right now, & the question keeping you up at night. No agenda beyond that. Just the people best equipped to see what's coming, comparing notes before it arrives. // ABOUT OBVIOUS Obvious is an applied AI research lab. We spend our days closing the gap between what's possible & what's doable, treating our own company as the experiment for what it means to operate at agent scale. We've reinvented our product, reshaped our team, accelerated revenue, & 10x our shipping velocity in less than a year.

jc_culture_10004817_2026_09_11_the_socie.summary: 91st Annual Members Exhibition The Society of American Graphic Artists (SAGA) is excited to announce its upcoming 91st Annual Members Exhibition, to be held at Mana Contemporary in Jersey City from September 11–27, 2026 (Fridays and Saturdays, 3:00–7:00 PM; Sundays, 12:00–3:00 PM). The Society of American Graphic Artists (SAGA) is a nonprofit organization established in 1915 whose mission is to promote contemporary printmakers, cultivate printmaking appreciation and education, and provide a collaborative and inclusive platform for artists across the country. https://sagaprints.com/ Hosting this year’s exhibition is Monira Foundation, an independent nonprofit institution that functions as a radical experimental laboratory, working in close collaboration with artists, curators, musicians, dancers, producers, and writers to conceive, realize, and present innovative projects in all media. Monira is located within Mana Contemporary, a 2-million-square-foot art center. The complex occupies a renovated 100-year-old former tobacco warehouse, featuring expansive exhibition spaces, working artist studios, the International Center of Photography archives, and more. A free public reception and awards ceremony with participating artists will be held on Saturday, September 26, from 3:00–5:00 PM. Guests are invited to enjoy light refreshments while celebrating the diversity and innovation of contemporary printmaking. jc_culture_10004818_2026_09_12_the_socie.label: Art / Culture
jc_culture_10004818_2026_09_12_the_socie.place: MANA CONTEMPORARY, 888 NEWARK AVE., JERSEY CITY
jc_culture_10004818_2026_09_12_the_socie.summary: 91st Annual Members Exhibition The Society of American Graphic Artists (SAGA) is excited to announce its upcoming 91st Annual Members Exhibition, to be held at Mana Contemporary in Jersey City from September 11–27, 2026 (Fridays and Saturdays, 3:00–7:00 PM; Sundays, 12:00–3:00 PM). The exhibition will feature 200 hand-pulled prints representing a broad range of printmaking techniques and subjects, created by SAGA artists from across the country. Awards will be juried by Leslie Diuguid, founder of Du-Good Press in Brooklyn. The Society of American Graphic Artists (SAGA) is a nonprofit organization established in 1915 whose mission is to promote contemporary printmakers, cultivate printmaking appreciation and education, and provide a collaborative and inclusive platform for artists across the country. https://sagaprints.com/ Hosting this year’s exhibition is Monira Foundation, an independent nonprofit institution that functions as a radical experimental laboratory, working in close collaboration with artists, curators, musicians, dancers, producers, and writers to conceive, realize, and present innovative projects in all media. Monira is located within Mana Contemporary, a 2-million-square-foot art center. The complex occupies a renovated 100-year-old former tobacco warehouse, featuring expansive exhibition spaces, working artist studios, the International Center of Photography archives, and more. A free public reception and awards ceremony with participating artists will be held on Saturday, September 26, from 3:00–5:00 PM. Guests are invited to enjoy light refreshments while celebrating the diversity and innovation of contemporary printmaking. WHEN Exhibition: Fridays–Sundays, September 11–27, 2026 Public Reception & Awards Ceremony: Saturday, September 26, 2026 3:00–5:00 PM WHERE Mana Contemporary 888 Newark Avenue Jersey City, NJ 07306

jc_culture_10003568_2026_09_16_hamilton_.summary: Join us at the Hamilton Park Farmers Market, your midweek destination for fresh, local, and thoughtfully crafted food and goods. Each week, we’re proud to feature farm-fresh produce from Stony Hill Farm alongside a curated selection of specialty vendors. Browse a variety of offerings including our long time vendor Pickles and Olives, fresh seafood from Scale Fish Market, and prepared foods perfect for dinner. You can also find baked goods, candles, personal care products, and more. You can even take advantage of convenient services like on-site knife sharpening while you shop. Whether you’re shopping for the week, grabbing a bite, or simply enjoying the park, the Hamilton Park Farmers Market is a welcoming space to connect with local vendors and neighbors.

jc_culture_10004827_2026_09_24_rent_the_.title: RENT: The Musical
jc_culture_10004827_2026_09_24_rent_the_.label: Music / Movies
jc_culture_10004827_2026_09_24_rent_the_.place: ART HOUSE, 345 MARIN BLVD, JERSEY CITY
jc_culture_10004827_2026_09_24_rent_the_.summary: Experience the groundbreaking Tony Award-winning musical and Pulitzer Prize-winning drama that defined a generation. Presented at Art House Productions during the 30th anniversary year of its original premiere, RENT follows a vibrant community of artists, musicians, and dreamers in New York City’s East Village as they pursue their passions, navigate love and loss, and strive to make a meaningful impact on the world around them. Set against the backdrop of the AIDS crisis, poverty, addiction, economic uncertainty, and a rapidly changing city, these artists discover the power of friendship, the importance of creative expression, and the enduring strength of community. Featuring iconic songs and an unforgettable rock score, RENT celebrates resilience, human connection, and the transformative role of the arts in times of hardship. This production is especially meaningful as part of Art House Productions’ 25th Anniversary Season. Founded in the wake of September 11, 2001, Art House was created to bring people together through the arts during a time of profound loss and uncertainty. Thirty years after its premiere, RENT remains as relevant, timeless, and inspiring as ever, reminding us all to measure our lives in love.
